workoutTypes.title: Workout types
workoutTypes.entryHint: What easy run, tempo, intervals & co. mean – and why they are in your plan.
workoutTypes.intro: Your calendar shows each session by its type. Tap a workout for the exact steps and targets; here you find what each type is for.

run.easy.name: Easy run
run.easy.description: Running at a pace where you can still hold a conversation – heart rate in Zone 2 (Zone 1 for recovery runs). Some easy runs end with strides: 15–20 seconds of relaxed, quick running.
run.easy.why: Builds your aerobic base, strengthens muscles and tendons and helps you recover. Most of your running should be easy.

run.long.name: Long run
run.long.short: Your longest run of the week, at an easy effort
run.long.description: A steady run clearly longer than your other runs, mostly in Zone 2. Go slower than you think – time on your feet counts, not pace.
run.long.why: Improves endurance and fat burning and gets body and mind ready for longer races.

run.tempo.name: Tempo run
run.tempo.description: After a warm-up you run one long block – or a few shorter ones – at threshold or race pace. Progression runs that get faster towards the end belong here too.
run.tempo.why: Raises the pace you can hold for a long time – the key for 10 km up to the marathon.

run.intervals.name: Intervals
run.intervals.description: Repeats of about 1–5 minutes at a hard effort – or a playful fartlek – with easy jogging in between, always with a proper warm-up and cool-down.
run.intervals.why: Improves your VO₂max, speed and running economy.

run.hills.name: Hills
run.hills.description: Short or long climbs run hard with easy recoveries on the way down – or steady hiking and running on steep terrain, plus downhill technique.
run.hills.why: Builds strength, power and running form with less impact than fast flat running, and prepares you for hilly races.

run.test.name: Test run
run.test.short: A benchmark that calibrates your zones
run.test.description: A time trial – e.g. 5 km or 30 minutes – at the best effort you can sustain. Your result updates your paces and zones.
run.test.why: Keeps your training targets right as you get fitter.

bike.easy.name: Easy ride
bike.easy.description: Steady riding in Zone 2 at a cadence that feels smooth. Recovery rides and bike commutes count as easy rides too.
bike.easy.why: Builds aerobic endurance with very little stress on your legs.

bike.long.name: Long ride
bike.long.short: Your longest ride of the week
bike.long.description: Hours in the saddle at an easy, steady effort. A good time to practise eating and drinking on the bike.
bike.long.why: Builds endurance for long events like a gran fondo or a triathlon.

bike.tempo.name: Tempo ride
bike.tempo.description: Longer blocks at an effort that needs focus but stays under control.
bike.tempo.why: Raises the power you can sustain on long rides.

bike.threshold.name: Threshold ride
bike.threshold.description: Blocks of about 8–20 minutes just below or at your threshold (FTP) with short recoveries.
bike.threshold.why: The most time-efficient way to lift your FTP.

bike.intervals.name: Intervals
bike.intervals.short: Hard efforts of a few minutes
bike.intervals.description: Repeats of about 2–5 minutes well above threshold with equally long recoveries.
bike.intervals.why: Improves your VO₂max and your ability to handle surges and short climbs.

bike.hills.name: Climbing ride
bike.hills.description: Seated and standing efforts on climbs – or high resistance on the indoor trainer.
bike.hills.why: Builds climbing strength and teaches you to pace long ascents.

bike.technique.name: Cadence drills
bike.technique.description: Easy riding with blocks of high and low cadence.
bike.technique.why: Makes your pedalling more efficient and coordinated.

bike.test.name: FTP test
bike.test.short: A benchmark for your power zones
bike.test.description: A 20-minute all-out effort after a thorough warm-up; about 95 % of the average power is your FTP.
bike.test.why: Keeps your power and heart-rate targets right.

swim.technique.name: Technique swim
swim.technique.description: Short repeats with drills for catch, kick and body position, with plenty of rest.
swim.technique.why: Better technique makes you faster with less effort – the biggest lever in swimming.

swim.easy.name: Easy swim
swim.easy.description: Steady swimming at a comfortable pace, a little slower than your CSS pace.
swim.easy.why: Builds swim endurance and feel for the water.

swim.threshold.name: CSS swim
swim.threshold.description: Repeats of 100–400 m at your Critical Swim Speed with short rests.
swim.threshold.why: Raises the pace you can hold over longer distances.

swim.speed.name: Speed swim
swim.speed.description: Sprints of 25–50 m with long rests.
swim.speed.why: Improves top speed and the power of your stroke.

swim.openwater.name: Open-water swim
swim.openwater.short: Practice for lakes and the sea
swim.openwater.description: Continuous swimming with sighting, swimming in a group and changes of pace.
swim.openwater.why: Prepares you for race conditions without lane lines and walls.

swim.test.name: CSS test
swim.test.short: A benchmark for your swim paces
swim.test.description: A 400 m and a 200 m time trial; together they give your Critical Swim Speed.
swim.test.why: Sets the paces of every swim session.

brick.brick.name: Brick
brick.brick.description: A ride followed immediately by a run, just like in a triathlon or duathlon.
brick.brick.why: Teaches your legs to run well after cycling.

strength.strength.name: Strength
strength.strength.short: Strength training that fits your plan
strength.strength.description: Your strength session – the Peakr programme, your own split or your own routine. The workout lists every exercise with sets, reps and rest.
strength.strength.why: Makes you more robust, prevents injuries and improves running economy. Heavy leg sessions are never placed right before a key session.

winter.easy.name: Winter endurance
winter.easy.description: Easy endurance on snow that replaces a run or ride with the same training load.
winter.easy.why: Real training in winter – full body and low impact.

winter.intervals.name: Ski intervals
winter.intervals.description: Repeats at a hard effort on cross-country skis.
winter.intervals.why: A strong aerobic stimulus that uses the whole body.

commute.commute.name: Commute
commute.commute.short: Getting to work by bike, running or on foot
commute.commute.description: Your regular trip to work or school, one way or there and back. Ridden, run or walked at an easy effort – no pace to hit.
commute.commute.why: Easy minutes that build your aerobic base without extra time. They count towards your training load, so the rest of the week is planned around them.

methodInfo.karvonen: Uses your heart rate reserve (max minus resting). More personal, because it reflects your fitness.
methodInfo.lthr: Zones from your lactate threshold heart rate (Joe Friel). The most precise if you know your threshold.

hr.autoMethod: Chosen automatically: Karvonen as soon as you enter your resting heart rate.
hr.hrMaxEstimateNote: Estimated from your age (208 − 0.7 × age). A measured value makes your zones more accurate.
hr.empty: Enter your age or max heart rate to see your heart rate zones.

run.title: Running pace zones
run.intro: Enter a recent race or all-out time trial. The more recent, the better.
run.thresholdNote: About the pace you could hold for one hour.
run.empty: Add a recent race result to get running pace zones.

swim.title: Swim pace (CSS)
swim.intro: Swim 400 m all-out, recover for 5–10 minutes, then swim 200 m all-out in the same pool. Enter both times.
swim.cssNote: Roughly the pace you can sustain for about 30 minutes.
swim.empty: Add a swim test to get swim pace zones.

errors.hrOrder: The lower limit must be below the upper limit.
errors.paceOrder: The slowest pace must be slower than the fastest pace.

trainingZones.saved: Saved. Your plan's targets now use these zones.
trainingZones.fixErrors: Please fix the highlighted fields before saving.

baseline.used: From your recent Strava activities: {{values}}. Used where you have not entered your own value.

hub.noSessions: No session logged yet. Start a routine or log a session.
hub.weekMuscles: This week: sets per muscle group

library.title: Exercise library
library.intro: Every exercise with how to do it, cues and the muscles it trains. Search by name, filter by movement or equipment.

exercise.title: Exercise
exercise.notFound: This exercise is no longer available.
exercise.copyIntro: Library exercises stay as they are. Change anything in your own copy – it shows up next to the original.
exercise.noHistory: You have not logged this exercise yet.
exercise.chartLabel: Estimated 1RM and heaviest set per session: {{values}}

edit.aliasesHint: Separated by commas – used by search and imports.

routines.deleteFolderHint: The routines in it are kept and move to "No folder".

starter.title: Start from a split
starter.intro: Ready routines to start with on day one. They land in their own folder – change anything you like.

import.title: Import from another app
import.intro: Bring your training history across with the CSV export your current gym app gives you – no paid plan or API key needed.
import.howToExport: Hevy: Settings → Export data. Strong: Settings → Export data. Other apps work too – you map the columns yourself.
import.empty: This file has no rows Peakr can read. Check that it is a CSV export.
import.noPreset: Unknown format – check the columns below.
import.createRoutines: Also create a routine for each workout name
import.doneSkipped_one: {{count}} workout was imported before and skipped.
import.doneSkipped_other: {{count}} workouts were imported before and skipped.

live.title: Session
live.emptyHint: Add the first exercise to start logging.
live.setTypeHint: Tap to switch between working, warm-up, drop and failure set. Long press removes the set.

finishEmpty.title: No set done yet
finishEmpty.body: Tick at least one set as done, or discard the session.

discard.title: Discard this session?
discard.body: Nothing of it will be saved.

running.title: A session is running
running.body: “{{title}}” is still open. Continue it, or discard it and start the new one.

rest.label: Rest after {{name}}
rest.doneBody: Time for your next set of {{name}}.

records.title: Personal records
records.oneRmNote: 1RM values are estimates (Epley formula, sets up to 12 reps), not tested maxima.

stats.title: Statistics
stats.frequencyAvg: {{value}} sessions per week on average over {{weeks}} weeks
stats.bodyMapLabel: Body map of the muscles trained: {{muscles}}
stats.nothing: No working sets this week yet.
stats.bandHint: The outlined range is the weekly target band (primary muscles count 1 set, secondary ½).

routes.title: Routes
routes.emptyHint: Import a GPX file (also from Komoot), plan routes in Strava, or let Peakr find the routes you run and ride most often.
routes.name: Name
routes.deleteMessage: “{{name}}” is removed from your library on all devices.

elevation.summary: {{gain}} m up, {{loss}} m down, between {{min}} and {{max}} m

climbs.title: Climbs
climbs.item: From km {{from}}: {{length}} m at {{avg}} % (max {{max}} %), {{gain}} m up

import.title: Import route
import.intro: Choose a GPX file or share one into Peakr. From Komoot: open the tour in the Komoot app, export it as a GPX file and share it with Peakr – name, distance and elevation are kept.
import.readError: The file could not be read. Is it a GPX file?
import.komootLink: This is a link to a Komoot tour. Peakr cannot read Komoot links. In the Komoot app, open the tour, choose “Export as GPX file” and share that file with Peakr.
import.notGpx: Peakr can import GPX files only. Share the route as a GPX file.

recognise.title: Routes from Strava
recognise.intro: Peakr looks at the runs and rides you recorded and suggests the routes you did at least twice. Your activities are only used for your own plan and library.
recognise.signIn: Sign in and connect Strava to find your routes.
recognise.failed: Strava could not be searched right now. Please try again later.
recognise.noneHint: Routes appear here once you recorded the same run or ride at least twice.
recognise.noElevation: Added without an elevation profile – Strava had no elevation data for it.

pace.primaryHint: Pace per km, adjusted to the gradient. Uphill slower, downhill at most a little faster.
pace.limitHint: Heart rate leads ({{hr}}). The pace per km is only a limit, adjusted to the gradient.

eval.title: Grade-adjusted evaluation
eval.inZone: {{share}} % of the time in the target zone

choose.title: Choose route
choose.intro: Pick a route for this session. Peakr adjusts the expected time and the pace per km to its hills.
choose.noOwn: No suitable imported route. Import a GPX file in Routes.
choose.freeHint: No route – just time and heart rate.
choose.fromHome: Routes near your home start point come first. Change it in Terrain profile.
choose.noStart: Set your home start point in Terrain profile to see routes near you first.

start.title: Home start point
start.hint: Where you usually start your runs and rides. Route suggestions prefer routes that start near it. Paste coordinates from a map app or use the start of one of your routes.
start.invalid: Enter latitude and longitude in degrees, e.g. 47.3769, 8.5417.
start.useRoute: Use the start of this route as my home start point
start.isHome: This route starts at your home start point.

location.explain: Or use where you are now: Peakr asks for location permission when you tap, reads your position once and saves it here. It does not track you.
location.denied: Location permission was not granted. Allow it in the system settings or enter coordinates instead.
location.unavailable: Your location could not be found. Check that location services are on, or enter coordinates instead.

generated.title: Generated round trips
generated.needStart: Peakr can plan round trips that fit this session from your home start point or from where you are now.
generated.none: No generated round trip fits this session from here.
generated.name: Round trip {{n}} · {{km}} km

error.offline: You are offline. Round trips are generated online.
error.limit: You have generated many round trips today. Try again tomorrow, or use your own routes.
error.subscription: Generated round trips are part of the Training subscription.
error.failed: Round trips could not be generated right now.

generated.attribution: Routes: openrouteservice.org by HeiGIT · Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors · Heights: {{heights}}
generated.attributionShort: Route generated with openrouteservice.org by HeiGIT · Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors

terrainProfile.title: Terrain profile
terrainProfile.intro: How hilly your training really is, learned from your outdoor runs and rides of the last 90 days. Peakr uses it to plan how hilly your sessions should be.
terrainProfile.adopted: Your plan now uses this terrain from today on.
terrainProfile.adoptFailed: The plan could not be updated (is it paused?).
terrainProfile.emptyHint: Connect Strava and record a few outdoor runs or rides – your terrain profile appears here.

baseline.referenceOnly: Reference only: these activities calibrate your plan. They are not added to your training history, load, records or completed sessions, and nobody else sees them.

step.title: Make my plan more accurate
step.body: Connect Strava and Peakr starts your plan from your recent training – your weekly volume, easy pace and heart rate – instead of estimates.
step.privacy: Peakr reads only runs, rides and swims from the last 60 days, nothing older. They are used for your own plan only and never to train AI.
step.used_one: {{count}} activity from the last 60 days calibrates your plan.
step.used_other: {{count}} activities from the last 60 days calibrate your plan.
step.reconnect: Your Strava connection was removed when you signed in to your existing account. Connect Strava again to calibrate your plan.

errors.denied: Strava access was not granted. You can try again or skip this step.
errors.error: Something went wrong. Try again or skip this step.
errors.rate_limited: Strava is busy right now. Try again in a few minutes or skip this step.

select.title: Your last 60 days
select.intro: Untick anything that does not show your usual training. Races and unusually long sessions are unticked already.
select.empty: No runs, rides or swims in the last 60 days. Your plan starts from your quiz answers.

outlier.race: Unticked: marked as a race on Strava.
outlier.muchLonger: Unticked: much longer than your other sessions.

summary.title: What Peakr derived
summary.intro_one: From {{count}} activity over {{weeks}} full weeks. Change anything that looks wrong – your entry always wins.
summary.intro_other: From {{count}} activities over {{weeks}} full weeks. Change anything that looks wrong – your entry always wins.
summary.volume: {{sessions}} sessions and {{minutes}} min a week, longest {{longest}} min
summary.cssHint: The 400 m / 200 m test in Training zones is more accurate.
summary.hrMaxHint: Your true maximum may be higher. Peakr uses it only when it is above the age estimate.
summary.restingHr: Resting heart rate is not available from Strava – enter it in Training zones.
summary.stravaZones: Your own heart-rate zones from Strava are used.
summary.stravaZonesScope: Reconnect Strava to use the heart-rate zones you set there.
summary.stravaZonesDefault: You use Strava’s default zones, so Peakr calculates your zones itself.
summary.weeklyLoadHint: Training load points (duration × zone). Week 1 starts here, within the time you have.
summary.notEnough: Not enough data ({{count}} of {{needed}} activities needed)

recalibrate.title: Recalibrate from recent activities
recalibrate.hint: Reads your last 60 days on Strava again. Reference only – nothing is added to your history.

zwift.howTo: Save the file in the Zwift workouts folder on your PC or Mac (Documents/Zwift/Workouts/<your Zwift ID>), then restart Zwift. The workout appears under Custom Workouts on all your devices.
zwift.error: The file could not be shared. Try again.

chip.noLocation: Set a location for the weather

hint.yourCall: Your call – nothing changes unless you choose an option.
hint.preferMove: This session doesn't translate well indoors, so another day is the better option.
hint.moveTo: Move to a dry day (the week is rebalanced)

alert.title: Today: {{workout}}
alert.move: you could move it to another day

settings.title: Weather check
settings.intro: Peakr checks the forecast for heavy rain, snow, ice and storms at your usual training time and suggests an indoor option or another day. You always decide.
settings.homeIs: Home start point: {{point}} – used when the current location isn't available.
settings.noHome: No home start point yet. Set one in Terrain profile so the weather check also works without location access.
settings.permissionDenied: No location access – the weather check uses your home start point instead.
settings.sessionHourHint: The forecast is checked for this time on each training day.
settings.attribution: Weather data: MeteoSwiss (Switzerland) and Open-Meteo.com, licensed under CC BY 4.0.

sleep_duration.label: Sleep
sleep_duration.about: Time asleep in the night that ended on this day, as recorded by your watch.

sleep_score.label: Sleep score (Garmin)
sleep_score.about: Garmin's own sleep score, shown as Garmin reports it.

hrv_night.label: Overnight HRV
hrv_night.about: Average heart rate variability measured while you slept.

resting_hr.label: Resting heart rate
resting_hr.about: Lowest steady heart rate of the day, as recorded by your watch.

stress_avg.label: Stress (Garmin)
stress_avg.about: Garmin's average stress level of the day on its own 0–100 scale.

intensity_min.label: Intensity minutes
intensity_min.about: Moderate minutes plus vigorous minutes counted twice, as Garmin counts them.

active_kcal.label: Active calories
active_kcal.about: Energy burned through activity on this day, as reported by the device.

resting_kcal.label: Resting energy
resting_kcal.about: Energy your body uses at rest on this day, as estimated by the device.

spo2_avg.label: Blood oxygen (SpO2)
spo2_avg.about: Average SpO2 reading of the day where your watch measured it.

respiration_avg.label: Respiration
respiration_avg.about: Average breaths per minute while awake.

weight.label: Weight
weight.about: From your connected scale or your own entries in the source app.

vo2max.label: VO2max (estimate)
vo2max.about: Your watch's VO2max estimate in ml/kg/min.

body_battery_high.label: Body Battery high (Garmin)
body_battery_high.about: Highest Body Battery value of the day, exactly as Garmin reports it.

body_battery_low.label: Body Battery low (Garmin)
body_battery_low.about: Lowest Body Battery value of the day, exactly as Garmin reports it.

sleep.title: Sleep
sleep.reads: Sleep duration, sleep stages, bed and wake time, Garmin sleep score

stress.title: Stress and Body Battery
stress.reads: Garmin stress level, Body Battery high and low

activity.title: Daily activity
activity.reads: Steps, floors, intensity minutes, active calories, VO2max estimate

body_comp.title: Body composition
body_comp.reads: Weight, body fat, muscle mass, BMI from a connected scale

womens_health.title: Women's health
womens_health.reads: Cycle tracking data. Off unless you switch it on. Peakr does not show it yet; switching it on only allows reading it once that view exists.

overview.title: Health
overview.historyFromConnection: Data starts on the day you connected – this Garmin connection does not deliver older days.
overview.backfilling: Fetching your older data – this can take a while.
overview.syncError: The last fetch did not work. Peakr tries again on its own.
overview.pushHint: New values arrive by themselves after your watch syncs with Garmin Connect.

baseline.building: Your usual range appears after {{needed}} days with data ({{count}} so far)
baseline.trendFlat: About the same as the 30 days before
baseline.ownHistory: Compared with your own history only – never with other people.

missing.not_connected: Connect Garmin or Health Connect to see this.
missing.not_permitted: Garmin is not allowed to share this with Peakr yet. Allow health data for Peakr in Garmin Connect under connected apps, then sync again.
missing.not_enabled: Not switched on. Turn on "{{group}}" in Health data settings.
missing.not_enabled_tile: Not switched on in Health data settings.
missing.not_provided: Your connected sources do not provide this.
missing.not_provided_garmin: Garmin does not provide this on Peakr's current Garmin access, and your phone's health store has no value for it either.
missing.syncFailed: The last fetch from Garmin did not work, so newer values may be missing. Peakr tries again on its own.

why.overnight: Nothing in the last {{days}} days. Your watch records this overnight – only on nights you sleep with it on – and sends it after it has synced.
why.continuous: Nothing in the last {{days}} days. Your watch records this all day while you wear it; values reach Peakr after the watch has synced with Garmin Connect.
why.spo2: Nothing in the last {{days}} days. Your watch measures this only if it has a Pulse Ox sensor and the Pulse Ox setting is on (all day or during sleep).
why.respiration: Nothing in the last {{days}} days. Only watches that measure breathing rate record this, while you wear them.
why.scale: No weigh-in in the last {{days}} days. Values come from a connected scale or an entry in Garmin Connect or Health Connect.
why.vo2max: No new estimate in the last {{days}} days. Garmin updates VO2max after outdoor runs with heart rate or rides with a power meter.

empty.title: Your body data in Peakr
empty.body: Connect Garmin to see sleep, HRV, resting heart rate, stress and more next to your training – compared with your own history.

detail.chartA11y: Line chart of {{metric}} over {{period}}: {{count}} values, latest {{latest}}.
detail.hardSessionsHint: Dips and rises often follow hard training. Each dot under the chart is one of these sessions.
detail.noHardSessions: No hard sessions in this period.
detail.consult: If this keeps up, talk to a doctor.

sleep.noStages: No sleep stages for this night.

body.title: Body composition
body.none: No scale measurements yet. Weigh in on a connected scale to see them here.

consent.title: Health data
consent.intro: Choose what Peakr may read. Each group is separate, you can switch it off at any time, and switching a group off deletes what Peakr stored for it.
consent.privacy: Your health data is stored encrypted, is never shown to anyone else and is never used to train models.
consent.saveError: Could not save. Check your connection and try again.
consent.garminComing: Garmin health data arrives once Garmin has approved Peakr.
consent.deviceBody: Reads the same groups from Health Connect on this phone (the last 30 days). The values stay on this phone. Garmin values win when both have one for the same day.
consent.deleteBody: Deletes every health value Peakr stored, on the server and on this phone. Your account, plan and connections stay.
consent.notPermitted: Not allowed at Garmin – allow health data for Peakr in Garmin Connect under connected apps.
consent.backfillBody: Fetches your Garmin history again, up to a year back. Use it if older days look incomplete.
consent.backfillStarted: Started. Older days fill in over the next hours.
consent.backfillError: That did not work. Try again later.

developer.title: Developer: Garmin personal API key
developer.body: For your own account only. Garmin's Personal API is meant for a person's own tools, so this stays a developer option. The key is sent to Peakr's server once, stored encrypted and never kept on this phone.
developer.connectedKey: Connected with a personal API key

errors.invalid_key: Garmin did not accept this key.
errors.already_connected: Garmin is already connected with OAuth.
errors.unavailable: Garmin could not be reached. Try again later.

recovery.confirmBody: Peakr eases today's session (shorter, lower intensity). You can change it back in the plan.
recovery.consult: If this keeps up, talk to a doctor.

diagnostics.title: Health sync details
diagnostics.intro: Developer view: what the last Garmin calls returned. Counts and status codes only, no values.
diagnostics.localEmpty: No health values stored on this device.
diagnostics.unavailable: The server details could not be loaded.

preview.title: Part of your subscription
preview.body: Your forecast and week 1 are free. The full plan – editing, routes, integrations, exports and your health data – starts with the 7-day free trial.

readOnly.title: Your plan is read-only
readOnly.body: Your subscription has ended. Your plan and history stay here; changes, routes, integrations and exports need an active subscription.

notifications.intro: At most one notification a day: in the morning on days with a planned workout, naming the session. Nothing on rest days.
notifications.signedOut: Sign in to get the reminder – it is sent from your account, so it also follows your plan from other devices.
notifications.denied: Notifications are turned off for Peakr in the system settings.

reminder.label: Daily workout reminder
reminder.hint: Sent at the time below in your current time zone, only on workout days.
reminder.weatherHint: When rain, snow, ice or a storm is expected around your session, the reminder says so and names the indoor option – in the same notification.
reminder.weatherOff: Turn on the weather check to get weather hints in the reminder.
reminder.title: Today: {{workout}}
reminder.body: Tap for the steps and targets.

activity.label: Synced activities
activity.hint: A notification when an activity from Strava or your watch arrives. Otherwise it only shows in the app.

units.label: Distances and paces
units.note: Heart rate, elevation gain and swim paces per 100 m stay as they are.

appearance.systemHint: Follows your phone: light by day, dark at night if it is set up that way.

haptics.title: Haptics
haptics.label: Haptic feedback
haptics.onHint: A short vibration when you complete a session or a set, and on the number keypad.

language.systemHint: Uses your phone's language when Peakr is available in it, otherwise English.
language.more: German, French, Italian and Spanish follow English.

privacy.stored: Your plan, settings and completed sessions live on this phone and in your Peakr account for sync and backup. Activities come only from services you connect.
privacy.never: Your data is never shown to anyone else, never sold and never used to train AI models.
privacy.connections: Connect or disconnect Strava and your watch; disconnecting deletes the imported data.
privacy.healthHint: Choose which body and recovery data Peakr reads, or delete all of it.
privacy.notifications: What Peakr may notify you about.
privacy.deleteHint: Removes your account and all its data for good.

bodyAddon.title: Body
bodyAddon.tagline: Food, check-ins and progress next to your training – so you see what your workouts add to your goal.
bodyAddon.trialActive: Free trial – nothing is charged until it ends.

benefits.diary: Food diary: everything you eat, by meal.
benefits.energy: Energy today: what is left, with the energy of today’s workouts added.
benefits.checkIn: Check-ins: weight and waist, read as a smoothed trend.
benefits.progress: Progress and coach: your trend over weeks, read against your training.

energy.title: Energy today
energy.fromWorkouts: +{{kcal}} kcal added back from today’s workouts
energy.estimate: Estimate from your profile and today’s planned sessions.
energy.floor: Today’s target is held at a safe minimum.
energy.setUp: Add your height, birth date and weight in Body to see this.
energy.intakeFrom: Intake from {{source}} (nothing logged in Peakr today).

diary.name: What
diary.incompleteHint: Incomplete days are left out of your maintenance estimate and the "calculation vs. scale" comparison.

checkIn.title: Check-in
checkIn.weighHintDaily: Weigh in whenever it suits you – several times a day is fine. The trend uses the day's value; day-to-day changes are mostly water.
checkIn.weighHintWeekly: You weigh in on your measuring day. Extra weigh-ins are welcome, never expected.

warning.outOfRange: This value is outside the usual range. Please check it.
warning.jump: That is a big change since last time. Please check the value – you can still save it.

quick.title: Daily kcal
quick.hint: Not logging food? Enter today's total here. Active kcal from your watch is optional.

checkIn.imported: Imported {{imported}} entries, skipped {{skipped}} (already there or without a date).
checkIn.photosNotImported_one: {{count}} photo could not come along – photos are not part of the backup file. Add them again in the check-in if you like.
checkIn.photosNotImported_other: {{count}} photos could not come along – photos are not part of the backup file. Add them again in the check-in if you like.
checkIn.importInvalid: This file is not a Körper-Tracker backup.
checkIn.deleteBody: The weigh-ins, measurements, photos and note of this day are removed. This cannot be undone.

form.bodyFatHint: From a scale or a measurement – used for fat vs. lean mass.
form.navyHint: US Navy formula from height, neck and waist (and hip for women). It is an estimate, often a few percent off.
form.navyMissing: Enter neck and waist (women also hip) and your height in the profile to get the estimate.
form.scaleMissing: No body fat value from a scale on this day.
form.measurementsHint: Same time of day, same conditions – ideally in the morning before eating.
form.photosHint: Private: only you can see them. Same place, light and pose each time.
form.photoPermission: Peakr needs access to the camera or your photos to add a progress photo.
form.invalidDate: Enter a date as YYYY-MM-DD, today or earlier.

neck.label: Neck
neck.how: Just below the larynx, tape level and snug but not pressing. Look straight ahead, shoulders relaxed.

waist.label: Waist (narrowest)
waist.how: At the narrowest point between the lowest rib and the hip bone, relaxed, after breathing out normally.

belly.label: Belly (navel)
belly.how: Horizontally at the level of the navel, standing upright and relaxed, after breathing out normally. Do not pull in.

hip.label: Hip (widest)
hip.how: Around the widest point of the buttocks, feet together, tape horizontal.

chest.label: Chest
chest.how: At nipple height under the armpits, arms hanging loosely, after breathing out normally.

shoulder.label: Shoulders
shoulder.how: Around the widest point of both shoulders, arms relaxed at your sides.

armL.label: Upper arm left
armL.how: At the thickest point of the upper arm, arm hanging relaxed (not flexed).

armR.label: Upper arm right
armR.how: At the thickest point of the upper arm, arm hanging relaxed (not flexed).

forearm.label: Forearm
forearm.how: At the thickest point just below the elbow, hand relaxed.

thighL.label: Thigh left
thighL.how: At the thickest point, about a hand's width below the crotch, weight on both legs.

thighR.label: Thigh right
thighR.how: At the thickest point, about a hand's width below the crotch, weight on both legs.

calfL.label: Calf left
calfL.how: At the thickest point of the calf, standing with weight on both legs.

calfR.label: Calf right
calfR.how: At the thickest point of the calf, standing with weight on both legs.

settings.title: Rhythm & reminder
settings.reminderHint: Sent at your daily reminder time. On days with a workout it is added to the workout reminder – never a second push.

checkIn.compareEmpty: Add photos to at least two check-ins to compare them.
checkIn.reminderLine: Measuring day: take a minute for your check-in.
checkIn.reminderBody: Take a minute for your check-in – weight, measurements, photos.

progress.title: Progress
progress.empty: Your trend starts with the first check-in.
progress.trendHint: A smoothed trend of your check-ins – single weigh-ins are mostly water and glycogen.
progress.tooFast: Your trend has fallen by more than 1.5 % of your weight in each of the last two weeks. That is faster than is easy to keep – consider eating a bit more.

coach.title: Weekly coach
coach.week: Looking back on the week of {{date}}
coach.progress: {{pct}} % of the way to your goal

numbers.balance: Balance: {{kcal}} kcal per day (≈ {{kg}} kg fat)

well.logging: You logged {{days}} of 7 days – that makes every number here more reliable.
well.onPace: Your trend moves at {{rate}} kg per week – right where you planned.
well.stable: Your weight is steady – exactly what maintaining means.
well.protein: Protein: {{grams}} g a day against a target of {{target}} g.
well.strength: {{sessions}} strength sessions – good for keeping muscle.

watchItem.fewLogs: Only {{days}} days were logged, so the energy numbers are rough.
watchItem.fastPace: Your trend is falling faster than planned ({{rate}} kg per week).
watchItem.fastPaceNoRate: Your trend is falling faster than planned.
watchItem.slowPace: Your trend moves slower than planned ({{rate}} kg per week).
watchItem.missedSessions: {{done}} of {{planned}} sessions done – a busy week happens.
watchItem.hardWeekAhead: This week's training is heavier than usual ({{share}} % of a typical week).

coach.noChanges: Keep going as you are – no change needed.

kcal.checkIn: Adjust your daily target by {{kcal}} kcal to match your planned pace.
kcal.tooFast: Eat {{kcal}} kcal more per day – a slower loss is easier to keep and protects muscle.

adjust.strength_one: Keep at least {{count}} strength session in the week.
adjust.strength_other: Keep at least {{count}} strength sessions in the week – they protect muscle while your weight changes.

coach.footer: Suggestions only – nothing changes until you accept it. Every number is an estimate.

teaser.title: Your weekly coach
teaser.body: See how your training affects your weight, energy and body – with clear suggestions each week.

profile.title: A few details first
profile.hint: Body needs these to estimate your energy. They are saved in your Peakr profile, so you enter them only once.
profile.invalid: Please check the values – one is outside the possible range.

readOnly.title: Body is read-only
readOnly.body: Your Body add-on has ended. Your diary, check-ins and progress stay here and can be exported; new entries need the add-on again.

export.failed: The export could not be shared. Please try again.

paywall.title: Unlock Body
paywall.onTop: An add-on to your Peakr subscription. Your training plan never depends on it.
paywall.trial: {{days}} days free. You enter your payment details now; the first charge comes only after the trial. Cancel anytime before it ends.
paywall.noTrial: Renews automatically. The free trial is once per account.
paywall.reactivate: Welcome back – everything you logged is still here.
paywall.bundleBody: Training and Body in one subscription, cheaper than both separately.
paywall.unavailable: Purchases are not available in this build.
paywall.failed: The purchase did not go through. You have not been charged.

balance.title: Energy balance (estimate)
balance.hint: Intake minus resting and active energy, on complete days only; 7,700 kcal ≈ 1 kg of fat.

tdee.title: Your maintenance (adaptive)
tdee.basis: From {{days}} logged days and your weight trend; the formula says {{formula}} kcal.
tdee.notYet: Needs 14 days with logged food and weigh-ins – {{days}} so far. Until then the formula estimate is used.

scale.title: Calculation vs. scale
scale.line: Expected {{expected}} kg, trend {{actual}} kg over {{weeks}} complete weeks.

confidence.low: Low confidence – only a little data so far.

scale.notEnough: Needs at least one complete week: all seven days logged and three weigh-ins. Days marked incomplete are skipped.

reason.matches: Calculation and scale agree – your log and the activity estimate fit well.
reason.underLogged: Some food may be missing from the log (snacks, drinks, oils, weekends).
reason.overLogged: Portions may be logged higher than eaten.
reason.activeOverestimated: The activity energy may be too high – a lower correction factor would fit better.
reason.activeUnderestimated: The activity energy may be too low – you may move more than the watch counts.
reason.water: Water and glycogen shift the scale by 1–2 kg without any fat change (salt, carbs, hormones, hard training).
reason.fewWeeks: Only a few complete weeks so far – the comparison gets more reliable over time.

composition.title: Fat and lean mass (estimate)
composition.current: Now: {{fat}} kg fat · {{lean}} kg lean mass
composition.change: Since your first measurement: fat {{fat}} kg · lean {{lean}} kg
composition.estimate: Body fat scales and measurements are approximate – read the direction, not the decimal.
composition.notEnough: Not enough data: add a body fat % in a check-in or connect a smart scale.

health.title: {{store}}
health.intro: Body can read {{list}} from your phone. You choose in the next step; nothing else is read.
health.privacy: The values stay on this phone and are never shared. Withdraw access any time in the system settings.
health.writing: Your diary is saved to {{store}} too – without counting it twice.

goal.title: Weight goal
goal.locked: Setting a goal needs the Body add-on.
goal.none: No goal yet. Your targets stay at maintenance until you set one.
goal.fromTrend: From your weight trend – not a single weigh-in.
goal.aboveMax: Not available: above 1 % of your weight per week (max {{max}} kg/week).
goal.floor: Held at your minimum of {{kcal}} kcal per day – that gives a realistic pace of {{rate}} kg/week.
goal.basisAdaptive: Based on your adaptive maintenance of {{kcal}} kcal.
goal.basisFormula: Based on the formula estimate of {{kcal}} kcal until there is enough data for your own.
goal.summaryChange: From {{from}} kg to {{to}} kg at {{rate}} kg/week.
goal.eatBackHint: Share of your completed workouts’ energy added to the day’s target.
goal.dailyHint: Each day has the same base; completed workouts add energy back.
goal.weeklyHint: Same weekly total, more on planned training days and less on rest days.
goal.paused: Your goal is paused – your targets are at maintenance.
goal.planned: Goal date at your chosen pace: {{date}}
goal.realUnknown: Your real pace shows after two weeks of weigh-ins.

checkIn.tooFast: This week: faster than planned ({{rate}} kg/week). A little more food keeps it sustainable.
checkIn.tooSlow: This week: slower than planned ({{rate}} kg/week). A small change can help – or give it another week.

goal.plateau: Your trend has not moved for three weeks although your log shows a deficit. Check how accurately you log (portions, drinks, oils) – or take a 1–2 week break at maintenance.
goal.reached: You have reached your target. Switching to maintain is a good next step.
goal.reverse: A reverse diet brings you back to maintenance in {{weeks}} weeks, +{{step}} kcal per week.

training.highLoad: A heavy training week – a smaller deficit (about {{kcal}} kcal) supports your sessions.
training.raceWeek: Race week – eat closer to maintenance (about {{kcal}} kcal deficit at most).
training.taper: Taper week – a smaller deficit (about {{kcal}} kcal) helps you arrive fresh.

goal.keyDays_one: Your deficit is large for this week’s key session – consider eating more on that day.
goal.keyDays_other: Your deficit is large for this week’s {{count}} key sessions – consider eating more on those days.
goal.estimate: All targets are estimates and adapt as your data grows.

fuelling.before: Before: a carbohydrate-rich meal a few hours before can help you start well fuelled.
fuelling.during: During: many athletes take about {{min}}–{{max}} g of carbohydrates per hour in sessions over 2 hours.
fuelling.after: After: carbohydrates with some protein help you recover.
fuelling.note: General guidance, not a prescription – go by what works for you.

food.noResults: Nothing found. Create the food yourself – it is then always there.
food.offline: Offline – showing your own foods and products scanned before.
food.attribution: Product data from Open Food Facts (openfoodfacts.org), ODbL. You can correct any entry.

empty.recent: Foods you log show up here.
empty.favourites: Mark foods as favourites to find them here.
empty.custom: Foods you create show up here.
empty.recipes: Recipes you create show up here.

food.per100Full: Per 100 {{basis}}: {{kcal}} kcal · P {{p}} g · C {{c}} g · F {{f}} g
food.notFound: This food is not available any more.
food.correctHint: Your corrected version is saved as your own food and is used whenever you scan this barcode.
food.cameraWhy: To scan barcodes, Peakr needs the camera. It is only used on this screen.
food.scanHint: Hold the barcode inside the frame. EAN and UPC codes are read.
food.scanNotFound: Barcode {{code}} is not in Open Food Facts yet.
food.scanOffline: You are offline and barcode {{code}} has not been scanned before.
food.name: Name
food.totalWeightHint: Weigh the cooked dish – cooking changes the weight. Without it the raw weight is used.

chart.title: Weight trend
chart.a11y: Weight trend chart. Trend weight {{kg}} kg, {{change}} kg since start.

energy.a11y: Energy per week: resting and active energy as stacked bars, eaten energy as a line. The weekly numbers follow below.

indices.title: Body indices
indices.hint: Common reference values: BMI 18.5–25, waist-to-height below 0.5, waist-to-hip below 0.9 (men) / 0.85 (women). They describe proportions, not health – your trend matters more than a single number.

measurements.title: Measurements since start
measurements.empty: Your measurement trends start with the first check-in.

features.diary: Food diary with barcode scan, recipes and your own foods
features.energy: Real energy balance from what you eat and the workouts you do
features.goal: Weight goal with a safe weekly rate and protein target
features.checkIn: Weigh-ins, body measurements and private progress photos
features.dashboard: Trend, fat vs. lean mass and “calculation vs. scale”
features.coach: A weekly coach that combines your training with your body data
